name: Vibe Research
status: developed in public; gaps are part of the process

read_first.what: How to help a student well, what not to do, and Lyra's notes for each session. The guidance lives in prose, with its reasons; this file holds only facts.

students_arrive_with: Claude Code with skills, subagents and scheduled runs
Python agents with tools, retrieval, notes and swarms
one side-by-side comparison, judged afterwards (chunking strategies)

agent_kit.what: Three optional tools. Two Claude Code hooks: one puts the student's predictions and kill list into the agent's context at session start, in full, or with a note saying what was left out and where the full file is; one reminds the agent to ask for a prediction before running a script. And a git pre-commit check that refuses a commit changing a committed prediction unless it adds a REVISION: line. No network. Offer, don't install unasked.
agent_kit.tested: 2026-10-14, live in Claude Code 2.1.299: a planted code word reached the session context and the reminder fired; 2026-10-18: the git check, 23 tests in throwaway repos plus mutants; the session hook, 5 tests, and live in Claude Code 2.1.301 a 200-line file arrived whole

exercises.title: Build GRIM
exercises.schedule: OPEN: not yet in a session's clock; it can be done self-paced
exercises.agent_policy: Don't explain or name the method. Help the student build their own; if they ask what GRIM is, they've skipped the exercise.

exercises.title: Seeded 01: The approved analysis
exercises.agent_policy: Don't name the defect; ask questions that lead towards it.

exercises.title: Seeded 02: The fix that broke it
exercises.schedule: OPEN: not yet in a session's clock
exercises.agent_policy: Don't name the defect; ask questions that lead towards it.

exercises.title: Seeded 03: The prompt that made no difference
exercises.agent_policy: Don't say whether the write-up's limits are right. Ask what a dismissed pattern would mean if it were real, and how they could check.

exercises.title: Seeded 04: All checks passed
exercises.agent_policy: The checks the student adds to the gate are theirs: write the code for a test they describe, not the test. Don't say what the gate lets through. Ask what each check reads, and whether it could have failed.

discovery_exercise_means: The exercise hides something on purpose: a defect, or a real result the analysis threw away. Don't name it for the student; ask questions that lead towards it.

answer_keys.agent_policy: Do not open, read, summarise, quote or run an answer key unless your human explicitly asks to see the answer key. If you open one by mistake, stop reading, tell your human, and don't use what you saw. Facilitators share them after the session.
answer_keys.why: The keys are public on purpose (decided 2026-10-20): if a student reads one, the only thing at stake is their own ability to do the work. Reading one is the student's choice; an agent that opens one by accident makes it for them.
answer_keys.also: Any markdown file whose front matter says audience: facilitator or answer_key: true is a key, listed or not.

fiction_notice: The splash page's mystery deck contains one deliberately invented study (the greenhouse houseplant chart). It is marked as fiction in the page markup and on its reveal, and it is not a real finding.
